business_problem: Merck researchers need to navigate large data sets, refine hypotheses, and complete repetitive and differentiated analysis tasks more efficiently during drug discovery and development.
solution_summary: Merck Research Labs describes using large language model-based AI agents as an internal research assistance layer for drug discovery and development. According to the story, these agents combine LLMs, AI models, and tools so complex scientific work can be broken into manageable subtasks, planned iteratively, and executed across multiple specialized assistants. Merck says the approach helps researchers navigate large data sets, refine hypotheses, and automate repetitive work such as data cleaning and preliminary analysis before results are returned to scientists for higher-level interpretation and decision-making. The article positions the system as an augmentation of human researchers and as an extension of Merck’s existing AI/ML investments. It does not name external vendors, model platforms, storage systems, or serving infrastructure, so the disclosed implementation is limited to an internal agent-based orchestration pattern rather than a detailed architecture stack.
data_flow: Research data and scientific context are provided to LLM-based AI agents, which decompose drug discovery questions into subtasks, coordinate AI/ML tools for data cleaning and preliminary analysis, and return synthesized outputs to Merck researchers for hypothesis refinement and decision-making. The source does not disclose storage systems or downstream application endpoints.
business_outcome: Merck says the AI agents help accelerate drug discovery and development work by automating lower-level analysis tasks and increasing researcher speed at scale while keeping scientists in the decision loop.
architecture_clues: Agent-based AI combines LLMs, AI models, and tools to iteratively plan, execute, and optimize tasks.
The implementation is described as a set of specialized AI assistants supporting Merck Research Labs researchers.
The page references Merck's prior investments in AI/ML but does not disclose named platforms, regions, or infrastructure topology.
evidence_quotes: "These LLM-based multitaskers, often called AI agents, can execute different tasks simultaneously."
"Having a team of high-performing AI assistants that can each play different roles ultimately helps researchers at Merck Research Labs (MRL) focus on critical drug discovery and development."

"AI agents are emerging as a powerful tool for researchers and scientists to aid them in navigating the complexities of large data sets, refining hypotheses and executing both repetitive and differentiated tasks efficiently."
"Repetitive tasks, such as data cleaning or preliminary analysis, can be handled by AI agents, freeing our scientists to focus on higher level work and strategic decision making."
"Agents help capitalize on Merck’s long-standing investments in AI/ML by rapidly accelerating the speed of our human researchers at scale."
